added.$comment: The sheet's single pick or drop action, with pre-jacking complete. The matrix calls the configuration a latent fork.
The sheet states no 180° turn, so a reversal is two quarter turns. The matrix gives a 2.8 s 180° turn, and indexes speed on fork position rather than load: 4.5 m/s forks down, 2.0 m/s forks up.
The sheet's 'fork raise time (pre-jacking action)'. It names no heights, so min and max are our reading. No handoff adds it: the sheet's pick and drop are timed with pre-jacking complete.

added.$comment: The A5 tool gives the fork type as 'hooked boxes, 3-deep and within'; its depth table times a 2-deep pick at 23.59 s and a 3-deep one at 39.94 s, relocation included. Pick, drop and alignment are the DA50 spec sheet's rows 1, 2 and 8: 6.2 s is the single-deep 'Pick Single/Multi Container SD', and row 8 is the 'Level Alignment Scan'. The simulator scans before every fork insertion, as issue #262 decided; whether the scan belongs to the approach alone is still unconfirmed.

added: Bootstrap source: sim/dessim/tests/fixtures/robots/quicktron_a5.world.json. A VTM that rides the racking. Handling and alignment from the DA50 spec sheet (rows 1, 2 and 8), the figures Cencora runs; travel and lift from Quicktron's A5 efficiency calculation tool (04 A5效率计算工具 V1.0-20251127). The tool disagrees on handling: a shallow pick or place 4.0 s, a deep one 5.0 s, a relay (buffer) place or pick 4.0 s, and a distance-dependent walk to the buffer rack of about 1.93 s on its default layout. The project decided on 2026-09-04 to model the cycle's fixed part as 15.8 s (notes/457-findings-2026-09-04.md) without splitting it among these figures; this file keeps the 17.2 s they give, which Cencora's results depend on. No source gives the A5's dimensions.
